clue.text: Examiner made redundant it seems, unconditionally

definitions.meaning: an examiner who has lost the job would set no more tests: nobody is quizzed any longer
an idiom for 'without any conditions or inquiry'

explanation.surface: A paper-setter has been laid off, apparently, with no strings attached.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is whimsical: once the examiner is sacked, nobody puts any queries to the candidates.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes an offer or deal made with no inquiry or conditions attached, hence unconditionally.

clue.text: Gambler who hasn't been handled very well?

parts.note: something never touched or fingered has never been felt
one who bets is a better

explanation.surface: A punter who has never been manhandled is in excellent shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the gambler first, but the pieces go together the other way round. The question mark marks the idiom used as a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a cheerful reply meaning one is in excellent health, so very well indeed.

clue.text: Piece found in here, for example?

definitions.text: Piece found in here, for example?

parts.words: Piece found in here, for example?
parts.note: ER, the royal cipher for the monarch Elizabeth Regina, sits inside the word 'here'; the same royal is also a chess piece

explanation.surface: Asking whether a chess piece might be kept in this box.
explanation.walkthrough: ER (Elizabeth Regina) is a crossword convention for the monarch; it is literally found in hERe, and the same title names a chessman.
explanation.definitionFit: The most powerful chessman bears the royal title that ER abbreviates, a female monarch.

clue.text: Charm of European road crossing country after taking a spin

indicators.note: spinning round turns the whole assembled road and country back to front
the road is said to cross the country, so it lies across and around it

parts.note: rue is the French word for street, a road on the Continent
Oman is a country in Arabia

explanation.surface: The charm of a Continental highway that runs through a land, once you have gone for a drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European road' is a French street, not an E-number motorway; 'crossing' and 'after taking a spin' together give RUOMANE read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamour someone is to captivate or charm them; both verbs mean win affection.

clue.text: Tile, useful thing that's pressed on towards the ceiling

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading upward means reading the letters from bottom to top
the word 'on' is pressed into the useful thing, squeezed inside it

parts.note: an asset is something of value or use
re means on or about, as in a memo heading

explanation.surface: A tile, a handy object stuck up overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'towards the ceiling' means upward, so ARESSET ('pressed' at work) is read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one small square piece of a mosaic, a little tile.

clue.text: Running desperate here, so piddling

parts.note: a machine that is running is on

indicators.note: desperate signals a frantic, disordered rearrangement of the following words

explanation.surface: A desperate race being run here, which makes it rather trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' looks like the start of the anagram, but it is the separate piece; 'desperate' acts only on 'here, so'.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-horse town is small and insignificant, so the term means petty or trifling.

clue.text: Opening letters from CID, a line is infuriating criminal

indicators.note: infuriating suggests letters driven mad and jumbled into a new order

parts.note: a fence is a criminal who receives and sells stolen goods

explanation.surface: Police detectives write to a crook who is enraging them with a single line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infuriating' shuffles CIDALINEIS into SICILIANDE, to which FENCE is added. CID is the British police detective branch; 'letters from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known chess opening, the set of first moves Black plays in reply to 1 e4.

clue.text: Significant moment, dad carrying baby before adoption

indicators.note: before places the father ahead of the adoption piece in the answer

parts.note: a woman carrying a baby is pregnant
pa is an informal word for father
adopting a method is putting it to use

explanation.surface: A father expecting a child ahead of an adoption.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants a family story; 'adoption' here means taking something into use.
explanation.definitionFit: A silence heavy with meaning, a deliberate halt in speech, is a significant moment.

clue.text: Noises from Centaurs, for example, where sauce and honey fed to Polyphemus?

indicators.note: the two pieces are fed into the giant, placed inside him

parts.note: Polyphemus is the one-eyed giant of the Odyssey, a Cyclops
lip, like sauce, means cheek or impudence
pet is a term of endearment, like honey

explanation.surface: Asks where cheek and a sweet treat were served to the one-eyed giant of Greek myth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed to' puts LIPPET inside CYCLOPS, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Centaurs are half horse, and the sound of hoofs on a road is described with this imitative word.

clue.text: Nice place, one captured by painter

indicators.note: the numeral is held inside the painter's name, as if caught

parts.note: Diego Rivera was a Mexican painter and muralist
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A pleasant spot, someone taken prisoner by an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the adjective but is the French city of Nice, which lies on the French coast in question.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice is a resort on the French coastal strip of that name, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Design cut out, street artist's tool blunted?

indicators.note: a blunted tool has lost its point, so its leading letter goes

parts.note: a pencil is a drawing tool for an artist

explanation.surface: A street artist's sharp instrument has lost its edge.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests graffiti, where stencils are indeed used, but 'blunted' strips the front letter from the drawing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a sheet with a pattern cut out of it, through which paint is applied.

clue.text: Soldier on with alder sculpting ornament with branches

parts.note: GI is an American enlisted soldier

indicators.note: sculpting shapes material into a new form, so these words are remoulded

explanation.surface: A soldier persists, carving wood from an alder into a decorative piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier on' looks like a phrasal verb meaning persist, but it splits: the soldier, then 'on' joins alder as fodder for 'sculpting'.
explanation.definitionFit: A girandole is a branched candlestick or ornamental bracket holding several lights.

clue.text: Bloomer, very big one breaking heart in metropolis

indicators.note: the size and the numeral break into the central letters, splitting them
the heart of a word is its central pair of letters

parts.note: XL is the clothing size extra large
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A huge blunder bursting into the centre of a big city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart in' takes OP from the middle of metropolis, and 'breaking' splits it around XLI.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxlip is a wild flower related to the primrose, and a flower is a bloomer.

clue.text: Peak with unidentified primate?

parts.note: an ape is a primate
X stands for an unknown or unnamed quantity

explanation.surface: A mountain top with a mysterious ape on it, perhaps a yeti.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or summit of something, its top.

clue.text: Sheets say on end of bed in illusionary realm

indicators.note: on places the sheets and the saying after the bed's final letter in this across entry
the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: a ream is a bundle of 500 sheets of paper
to state is to say

explanation.surface: Bedsheets are talked about at the foot of a bed in a fantasy world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheets' suggests bedding to go with the bed, but here it is paper counted in reams.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamlike condition is a world of illusion, apart from reality.

clue.text: Butcher saving me — from this?

indicators.note: to butcher is to hack apart, so the words that follow are chopped and reordered

explanation.surface: An animal hopes the butcher will spare it, wondering what lifestyle might save it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher' rearranges SAVINGME. Read whole, the clue is an animal's plea: a meat-free diet would keep it from the butcher.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes the practice of eating no animal products, which spares livestock from slaughter.

clue.text: Short distance when knocked over caught by punch — as far as possible

parts.note: a short is a small measure of spirits, a tot

indicators.note: the distance is caught, held inside the punch

parts.note: to punch is to hit

indicators.note: knocking something over turns it upside down, so the distance is read backwards

parts.note: a mile is a distance

explanation.surface: A small gap, once toppled, ends up taking a blow, going to the extreme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like an adjective for distance but is the noun for a dram of spirits; 'when knocked over' gives ELIM, which 'caught by' places in the punch.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to the utmost extent, as far as one can go.

clue.text: Could supporter be on tour of a hot city in Iran

indicators.note: touring something means going round it, so the supporter piece encircles the rest

parts.note: the question 'is fan...?' asks whether someone could be a supporter
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a fan might travel around a hot Iranian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on tour of' puts A and H inside ISFAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Isfahan is a historic Persian city in central Iran, famous for its mosques.

clue.text: Cocktail of deceit with a drink

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these words are mixed together

explanation.surface: A cocktail made of trickery served alongside a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cocktail of' mixes DECEITA into ICEDTEA; 'with' is a link joining the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilled tea served over ice is a refreshing beverage, a drink.

clue.text: Bedtime companion who's stuffed, head ripped off in vortex

indicators.note: ripping off the head removes the first letter

parts.note: a teddy bear is a stuffed toy taken to bed

explanation.surface: A stuffed toy decapitated in a whirlpool, a sad bedtime tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who's stuffed' sounds like a jibe at an overfed person, but it is the soft toy.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirl of water or air, a small whirlpool.

clue.text: Character of Mr. Kipling's cake, layered jams

indicators.note: jams means packs in tightly, so these words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: Mr Kipling, a British cake brand, makes a layered cake with jam fillings.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Kipling is a British brand of packaged cakes; the definition instead means the author Rudyard Kipling. The run spans 'cAKE LAyered'.
explanation.definitionFit: Akela is the wolf pack leader in Kipling's Jungle Book, one of his characters.

clue.text: Payment admissible, experience nausea?

parts.note: a fee is a payment
something lawful is allowed, admissible

explanation.surface: Asking whether an acceptable charge could make one sick.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel sick is one way of being unwell, so nausea is an example; hence the question mark.

clue.text: See 1 Across
Drunk son has too much, and I don't say a word!

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means excessive
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A drunken son overindulges and a parent vows silence.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT is British shorthand for over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Sottish describes someone stupefied with drink, a sot.

clue.text: Adopted sheep assimilating a range of knowledge

indicators.note: assimilating takes something in, so the ram holds the other pieces

parts.note: a tup is a ram
one's ken is the range of what one knows

explanation.surface: A sheep that was taken in absorbs some learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assimilating' puts AKEN inside TUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobby or idea that is adopted is one that has been taken up.

clue.text: Brilliant autumn entertainer with line in book

indicators.note: the two pieces go in, inside the book

parts.note: a romance is a novel, a book
and means with or plus

explanation.surface: A dazzling performer of autumn has a line in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Fireworks are an autumn entertainment in Britain on Bonfire Night, 5 November. 'in' puts ANDL inside ROMANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: This firework shoots out bright balls of fire, a dazzling show for autumn displays.
